A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DHTM research, despite the title changing from Successor Representations to Successor Features. The complete text, equations, figures and appendices support comparison; the experiments are substantially revised.

before.justification: V1 reports original Pinball experiments measuring prediction surprise and adaptation after environmental changes, including a prediction-horizon comparison (Figures 3–4).

after.justification: V2 reports original navigation experiments in fully and partially observable Gridworld and in AnimalAI, with learning curves in Figures 3–5.

M1.justification: V1's agent explicitly learns SR through n-step TD and uses log reward priors for valuation. V2 specifies direct SF rollouts under a uniform future policy, adaptive stopping and linear feature-reward Q estimates (Section 3.3). The segment-likelihood computation also changes through an added mean-synaptic-efficacy multiplier (v1 Equation 11; v2 Equation 8), while the underlying Hebbian factor-graph memory remains.

E1.justification: The Pinball environment and its force-field scenarios are removed. V2 evaluates fully observable coordinate-based Gridworld, partially observable colour-based Gridworld, and first-person visual navigation in AnimalAI. These change the observation conditions, dynamics and navigation requirements.

E2.justification: V1 evaluates LSTM, RWKV and factorial CHMM against DHTM. V2 removes RWKV from experimental comparisons and introduces Q-table and SR-table agents in fully observable Gridworld (Figure 3). LSTM remains in partially observable Gridworld (Figure 4), and the clone-HMM comparison lineage continues through CSCG, with a differently described implementation.

E3.justification: V1 measures prediction surprise and reward using short Pinball episodes and one-/five-step TD predictions. V2 measures steps to the goal and introduces trajectory-buffer refresh and change-oracle protocols. Planning uses ten steps in fully observable Gridworld and adaptive horizons up to 50 elsewhere, with respective discounts of 0.99 and 0.8 (Appendix D). These are replacement experimental protocols.

E4.justification: V1's explicit one-versus-five prediction-step ablation is removed. V2 instead compares CSCG with and without an environmental-change oracle in both Gridworld settings, testing whether renewed random-policy data collection restores adaptation (Figures 3–4). This changes the central diagnostic question from prediction horizon to training-data refresh.

E5.justification: V1 reports averaging three trials and displays shaded bands without identifying their statistical meaning. V2 explicitly reports at least five differently seeded runs per setup and identifies the displayed variation as standard deviation. This describes the new evaluations, not additional runs of the earlier Pinball experiments.

E6.justification: The Pinball surprise and adaptation results are replaced by navigation results. V2 reports faster Gridworld adaptation than CSCG, approximately 13 steps versus a nine-step optimum after the partially observable maze changes, and stable AnimalAI goal reaching after about 150 episodes. AnimalAI baseline training failures are also reported. These findings cannot establish same-setting performance gains over v1.

T1.justification: The mathematical revisions are localized: Section 2.3 changes SR from finite-horizon observation occupancy to infinite-horizon future-state occupancy; Appendix B adds a feature-additive reward approximation and value decomposition. V2 Equation 8 also revises the segment-likelihood interpolation. The underlying factor-graph formulation remains, without a new theorem or proof framework.

C1.justification: The principal empirical claim shifts from accurate SR predictions and faster TD learning in Pinball to online SF-based navigation and adaptation relative to LSTM and CSCG. V2 drops the advertised HMM-version-of-RNN contribution and adds claims about long-horizon belief propagation and neuromorphic implementation. The core contribution of local Hebbian temporal memory remains.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantial discussion of fast learning versus weak trajectory generalization, correlated-buffer overfitting, and encoder non-stationarity as a possible explanation for AnimalAI baseline failures. It qualifies that LSTM/CSCG are not inherently incapable of solving the tasks and proposes a future fast/slow hierarchy. These interpretations and limitations extend well beyond v1's encoder caveats.

D1.justification: V1 mainly documents the encoder and a brief experimental setup. V2 adds explicit Hebbian update formulas, baseline architectures and training regimes, buffer sizes, validation rules, DHTM dimensions, initialization, learning rates, pruning and planning thresholds (Appendix D). It also details preprocessing and environment interaction and supplies a source-code access link; the link's availability was not independently verified.

R1.justification: V2 adds targeted references and connections concerning successor features, episodic memory, cortical layers, AnimalAI and baseline implementations, including Gershman, Touati et al., and Staiger and Petersen. Godot and several earlier cortical-model references disappear. The principal positioning around Factorial HMMs, world models and local Hebbian learning is retained.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, agent explanation and conclusion are substantially rewritten around SF-based planning. Methods is reorganized into factor-graph, neural-implementation and agent subsections. The single encoder appendix becomes part of an A–F appendix structure with dedicated explanations and a glossary; the original encoder discussion is largely retained.

P2.justification: V1's compact three-panel method figure is replaced by separate, expanded factor-graph and neural-implementation diagrams, plus a new biological illustration. Pinball screenshots and plots disappear, replaced by larger Gridworld/AnimalAI learning curves and new environment illustrations (v2 Figures 3–9). This substantially revises the visual organization.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially improves assessability and reproducibility through explicit learning rules, baseline training details, uncertainty definitions and implementation information. Its comparative Gridworld navigation tests and oracle controls address adaptability more directly than v1's prediction comparison and DHTM-only horizon ablation, while new limitations constrain interpretation. Losing the predictive-surprise and horizon analyses, and lacking successful AnimalAI baseline curves, narrows some evidence, but the methodological transparency and more direct validation provide a substantial net improvement.
